answers.q1: Maven, using the checked-in wrapper (a Gradle build also exists, but the Maven wrapper is the primary one). Install dependencies with: ./mvnw dependency:resolve (or ./mvnw -B compile). Maven has no separate install step. Dependencies are also fetched automatically by any ./mvnw build.
answers.q2: ./mvnw test (CI runs the full build with ./mvnw -B verify, which includes the tests and the format and checkstyle validation). The Gradle equivalent is ./gradlew test.
answers.q4: CI runs ./mvnw -B verify. Its validate phase runs spring-javaformat:validate and the nohttp checkstyle check. To run only those, use: ./mvnw -B validate. To fix formatting, run ./mvnw spring-javaformat:apply. The Gradle workflow runs ./gradlew build.
answers.q5: src/main/resources/static/resources/css/petclinic.css is generated from src/main/scss/ plus Bootstrap, via ./mvnw package -P css. Edit the scss and regenerate instead of editing the CSS by hand. The vendored font files in src/main/resources/static/resources/fonts/ and the Gradle and Maven wrapper files (gradle/wrapper/*, .mvn/wrapper/*, gradlew, gradlew.bat, mvnw, mvnw.cmd) should not be hand-edited either. target/ and build/ are build output and are not checked in.
